comment: Application profile (DCMI sense) for personal-conversation memory: 9 classes and 25 object properties, hand-assembled from schema.org (20 properties, all 8 reused classes), the Relationship vocabulary (2 properties) and 3 terms invented here because no surveyed vocabulary has an equivalent. Rationale, citations and the term-by-term argument: docs/research/2026-08-01-personal-memory-graph-vocabulary.md. This is the RELATION vocabulary only - entity typing stays on the full schema.org digest, which does that job well. Every property declares a domain and a range naming a class in this file, because that is what selects it: the entity TYPES a chunk yields evoke the properties whose endpoints they satisfy. Hand-written rather than generated by python -m processrecall.ontology.digest: there is no single RDF source to parse, and 34 curated rows are the deliverable. Deviations from the research note, all deliberate: sdo:startDate/sdo:endDate are dropped (their range is a datatype, and dates never become REL endpoints here - they live on TEMPORAL/MENTIONS_DATE), prov:wasDerivedFrom is dropped (provenance is an edge attribute we already carry, not a relation between two extracted entities), and gk:Preference is dropped (no property ranges over it and nothing can extract it, so it would be a dead label). sdo:owns ranges over Product ALONE, not Product+Thing: a range containing Thing admits every entity including people, which switches off the one violation the range gate enforces (`Jon owns students`, and `has`->owns turning `my sister Maria` into a possession).

classes.label: Thing
classes.definition: The most generic type of item.

classes.label: Person
classes.definition: A person (alive, dead, undead, or fictional).

classes.label: Organization
classes.definition: An organization such as a company, school, NGO, club, team or support group.

classes.label: EducationalOrganization
classes.definition: An organization that provides training or education, such as a school, college or university.

classes.label: Place
classes.definition: Entities that have a somewhat fixed, physical extension, such as a city, a neighbourhood, a home or a venue.

classes.label: Event
classes.definition: Something that happens at a particular time and place, such as a trip, a wedding, a concert or a performance.

classes.label: Occupation
classes.definition: A profession or role a person holds, such as nurse or teacher, independent of any particular employer.

classes.label: Product
classes.definition: Something owned, made, grown or bought: a possession, a vehicle, a pet, a piece of a collection.

properties.label: knows
properties.definition: The most generic bi-directional social or work relation: the subject knows this person, with the bond left unstated.

properties.label: friendOf
properties.definition: The subject considers this person a friend.

properties.label: spouse
properties.definition: The person the subject is married to.

properties.label: lifePartnerOf
properties.definition: The subject's unmarried long-term or live-in partner.

properties.label: parent
properties.definition: A parent of the subject: their mother or father.

properties.label: children
properties.definition: A child of the subject: their son or daughter.

properties.label: sibling
properties.definition: A brother or sister of the subject.

properties.label: relatedTo
properties.definition: The most generic familial relation: a cousin, aunt, uncle, grandparent, in-law or other relative.

properties.label: colleague
properties.definition: A person the subject works with.

properties.label: worksFor
properties.definition: The organization the subject works for.

properties.label: memberOf
properties.definition: A club, team, support group or other organization the subject belongs to.

properties.label: hasOccupation
properties.definition: The profession or role the subject holds, such as nurse, teacher or designer.

properties.label: alumniOf
properties.definition: A school, college or university the subject studied at.

properties.label: homeLocation
properties.definition: Where the subject lives.

properties.label: workLocation
properties.definition: Where the subject works.

properties.label: nationality
properties.definition: The country the subject is a national of.

properties.label: owns
properties.definition: Something the subject owns or possesses.

properties.label: knowsAbout
properties.definition: A topic, subject or skill the subject is knowledgeable or experienced about.

properties.label: likes
properties.definition: Something the subject likes, enjoys or is a fan of. Invented term: schema.org has no like property on Person, and foaf:interest ranges over Document, which would need a document minted per preference.

properties.label: dislikes
properties.definition: Something the subject dislikes, avoids or complains about. Invented term: no surveyed vocabulary has a dislike property, and adversarial questions turn on it.

properties.label: plansTo
properties.definition: Something the subject intends, plans or hopes to do. Invented term: no goal or plan predicate exists in schema.org, FOAF, the Relationship vocabulary, BIO or PIMO.

properties.label: lifeEvent
properties.definition: A significant biographical occurrence in the subject's life, such as a wedding, a move, a graduation or a bereavement.

properties.label: attendee
properties.definition: A person who attended or took part in the event.

properties.label: location
properties.definition: Where the event took place.

properties.label: about
properties.definition: What the event was about or concerned.
